commitResults.messageBody:
Align the task manager code with the project’s Java conventions.

Add package declarations and Javadocs, improve field encapsulation,
standardize method naming, and clean up whitespace and brace formatting.

Separate command processing into helper methods so each method operates at
a single level of abstraction.

Document the purpose, parameters, and return values of methods in MimiMeow.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for todo, deadline, and event commands
Add task inheritance for todo deadline and event
commitResults.messageBody:
Make Todo, Deadline, and Event extend Task and store them through
the common Task array. Update command handling to construct the
appropriate task subtype and use polymorphic string formatting.

Display the added task and update the user with the current number
of tasks in the list.

The mark and unmark commands duplicated task lookup, bounds checking, and response output. This duplication made the two command paths harder to keep consistent as the task-status behavior evolves.\n\nCentralize the shared workflow in updateTaskStatus and keep only the status-specific mutation and message in one conditional. This preserves existing behavior while giving future status-related changes a single implementation point.

MimiMeow directly owned the task array and its mutable count, making the command-line UI responsible for both presentation and storage internals. This global state increased coupling and made changes to task storage harder to contain.\n\nIntroduce TaskList as the single owner of task storage, including its capacity, array, and count. MimiMeow now interacts with that state through add, size, and get operations, preserving existing behavior while improving information hiding and keeping responsibilities focused.
